question: A 66-year-old man comes to the physician because of difficulty walking for the past year. He reports that his gait has become slower and that initiating steps has become more challenging. During the past 6 months, his family has noticed that he is starting to forget important family meetings and holidays. On a number of occasions, he has not been able to get to the bathroom in time in order to urinate. He has hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide. His father died of Parkinson's disease at the age of 63 years. The patient had smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years, but quit 10 years ago. His vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he is confused and has short-term memory deficits. He has a wide-based, shuffling gait. Muscle strength is normal. Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally. An MRI of the head is shown. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.ope: Degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the temporal lobe

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "66-year-old man with difficulty walking" -> "slower gait and challenging initiation of steps" -> "possible neurodegenerative disorder" -> "family history of Parkinson's disease" -> "cognitive decline and memory deficits" -> "wide-based, shuffling gait" -> "possible normal pressure hydrocephalus" -> "obstructed passage of cerebrospinal fluid" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has confusion and short-term memory deficits" -> "indicates possible cognitive impairment" -> "wide-based, shuffling gait suggests movement disorder" -> "family history of Parkinson's disease raises suspicion" -> "MRI findings likely show ventricular enlargement" -> "suggests possible obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid" -> "decreased absorption of cerebrospinal fluid" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient's symptoms include urinary incontinence" -> "suggests possible neurological involvement" -> "difficulty walking and cognitive decline" -> "could indicate normal pressure hydrocephalus" -> "which is associated with obstructed cerebrospinal fluid flow" -> "leading to symptoms of gait disturbance and cognitive issues" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of smoking and hypertension" -> "risk factors for vascular issues" -> "could contribute to cognitive decline" -> "but family history of Parkinson's is significant" -> "indicating a possible neurodegenerative process" -> "leading to degeneration of cholinergic neurons" -> "in the temporal lobe" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including difficulty walking, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence, suggest a diagnosis of normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH). NPH is characterized by the triad of gait disturbance, cognitive dysfunction, and urinary incontinence, often associated with an obstructed passage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leading to ventriculomegaly. The MRI findings would likely show enlarged ventricles with normal ventricular pressure, supporting this diagnosis. Therefore, the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms is obstructed passage of cerebrospinal fluid.
